--- title: "Files & Data Manipulation" --- ## Reading and Writing Files ### Text Files ::: {#2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} # Writing to a file open("example.txt", "w") do f write(f, "Hello, Julia!") end # Reading from a file content = read("example.txt", String) println(content) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Hello, Julia! ``` ::: ::: ### CSV Files ::: {#4 .cell execution_count=0} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using CSV, DataFrames # Read CSV df = CSV.read("data.csv", DataFrame) # Write CSV CSV.write("output.csv", df) ``` ::: ## DataFrames DataFrames are tabular data structures similar to pandas in Python or data.frames in R. ### Creating DataFrames ::: {#6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using DataFrames # Create from columns df = DataFrame( name = ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"], age = [25, 30, 35], city = ["Helsinki", "Espoo", "Tampere"] ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Working with Geoscientific Data ### Loading Geophysical Data ::: {#16 .cell execution_count=0} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using DelimitedFiles # Read space-delimited data data = readdlm("gravity_data.txt") # Extract columns x, y, gz = data[:, 1], data[:, 2], data[:, 3] ``` ::: ### NetCDF Files ::: {#18 .cell execution_count=0} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using NCDatasets # Read NetCDF ds = Dataset("climate_data.nc") temp = ds["temperature"][:] close(ds) ``` :::
